actual_behavior_limitation: On a compiled-artifact cache hit, `mncs call` still spends ~8s (debug binary): cache-hit-load ~4.9s plus session-open ~3.0s re-validating the cached artifact and opening the session. The timed decide() execution itself is sub-second. Identical repeated calls therefore cost 8-9s warm instead of milliseconds.
alternatives_considered: debugger-side memoization of native answers (hides staleness; already exists as memo warm path)
current_workaround: Debugger narrows library roots and shares one cache directory so warm calls cost ~8s instead of 30-90s; memo layer avoids repeat questions within a session.
expected_semantics: A cache hit loads and validates in milliseconds: cheap integrity check over the cached bytes plus session open without full re-admission work. Repeated identical native calls cost ~1s or less even on debug builds.

host_language_code_required.why: No host code involved; the gap is validation cost inside the toolchain.

minimal_reproducer.command: MNCS_TIMINGS=1 mncs call <core> --module mncs.debug --function decide --args-json ... (twice; second run prints cache-hit-load/session-open stages)

proposed_primitive_or_semantic_direction: Validate cached artifacts incrementally (hash bytes once, trust validated structure) or split admission (full, on miss) from session open (cheap, on hit); measure with MNCS_TIMINGS on both build modes.
resolution_criteria: Two identical `mncs call` invocations: second completes in ~1s or less on a debug build with timings attributing hit-load plus session-open under that budget.
title: Native cache hits still cost ~8s in artifact validation and session open
why_capability_matters: Every native semantic/policy call in debug, test, Doctor, and Forge pays this warm cost; it dominates warm debugger interaction once cold compile is cached.
